% Pattern: kind/untitled. An environment with no title, numbered within the
% section, numbers the paragraphs of the paper. A paragraph that starts with
% a bold head, after its label, is an item of the kind of the head; one with
% no head is a numbered paragraph. Seen in the gold pilot (set X).
% want pkt-1 unknown 1.1
% want pkt-2 definition 1.2 labels=def
% want pkt-3 statement/proposition 1.3 status=here labels=prop
% want proof-1 proof - proves=pkt-3
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\newtheorem{pkt}{}[section]
\newcommand{\bpk}{\begin{pkt}\rm }
\newcommand{\epk}{\end{pkt}}
\begin{document}
\section{One}
\bpk
We recall the setting of the problem and the spaces that we use.
\epk

\bpk\label{def} {\bf Definition.}
A space is nice when it is compact.
\epk

\bpk \label{prop} {\bf Proposition.} {\em Every nice space is bounded.}
\begin{proof} Cover the space by balls. \end{proof}
\epk
\end{document}
